problem_text:
A distribution center must devise a procurement and stock management strategy for a critical component over a 6-week schedule.  
The starting stock at the commencement of the schedule is 59 units.  
In each week \( t = 1, \dots, 6 \), the vendor permits the center to submit a procurement request whose size must be between 1 and 71 units.  
Nevertheless, every request submitted requires a lead time of 3 weeks before the components become available to fulfill requirements or augment stock.  
The requirement for the component in each week is specified as follows:  
* Week 1: requirement 58 units  
* Week 2: requirement 10 units  
* Week 3: requirement 12 units  
* Week 4: requirement 41 units  
* Week 5: requirement 30 units  
* Week 6: requirement 29 units  

Stockouts are permissible, but any unfilled requirement will not be carried forward.  
Throughout the schedule, component quantities may be fractional, and the total quantity of physical stock on hand at any point must not surpass the storage limit of 59 units.  

In week 2, the maximum procurement quantity is restricted to 2 units.  
In week 4, the physical stock on hand must be no less than 43 units.  

The aggregate expense over the schedule comprises three elements: the procurement expense, which is 2 per unit requested; the storage expense, which is 3 per unit of stock held from one week to the next; and the stockout penalty, which is 7 per unit of unfilled requirement. Determine the optimal procurement quantity for each week and monitor the resulting stock and stockout levels so as to minimize the total expense.
